title: Romans Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Romans chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Romans Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Romans Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Romans 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
We are buried with him by baptism into death
Our old man is crucified with him
He that is dead is freed from sin
questions.correctAnswer: Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:1 begins with the question, 'What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?'

questions.question: According to Romans 6:2, how should those who are dead to sin live?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:2 says, 'How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?' implying we should not live in sin anymore.

questions.question: What are believers baptized into, according to Romans 6:3?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:3 states, 'so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death.'

questions.question: What does baptism symbolize according to Romans 6:4?
options: Being buried with Christ by baptism into death
questions.correctAnswer: Being buried with Christ by baptism into death
questions.explanation: Romans 6:4 says, 'Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death.'

questions.question: By what power was Christ raised from the dead as mentioned in Romans 6:4?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:4 states, 'like Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father.'

questions.question: What should believers walk in, according to Romans 6:4?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:4 says, 'even so we also should walk in newness of life.'

questions.question: What will believers be in the likeness of, according to Romans 6:5?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:5 states, 'we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection.'

questions.question: According to Romans 6:6, what happened to our old man?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:6 says, 'our old man is crucified with him.'

questions.question: What is the purpose of crucifying the body of sin, according to Romans 6:6?
options: That henceforth we should not serve sin
questions.correctAnswer: That henceforth we should not serve sin
questions.explanation: Romans 6:6 explains it is 'that henceforth we should not serve sin.'

questions.question: What is said about one who is dead, in Romans 6:7?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:7 states, 'For he that is dead is freed from sin.'

questions.question: If we are dead with Christ, what do we believe according to Romans 6:8?
options: That we shall also live with him
That we shall reign on earth
questions.correctAnswer: That we shall also live with him
questions.explanation: Romans 6:8 says, 'Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him.'

questions.question: True or False: Romans 6:3 teaches that baptism is into Jesus Christ's death.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:3 states, 'so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death.'

questions.question: True or False: Romans 6:7 says that one who is dead is freed from sin.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:7 clearly states, 'For he that is dead is freed from sin.'

questions.question: True or False: Romans 6 says that baptism is a symbol of receiving the Holy Spirit.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:3-4 describes baptism as being buried with Christ into his death, not as receiving the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 6 says we should live longer in sin because grace may abound.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:1-2 rejects the idea of continuing in sin to make grace abound.

medium.title: Romans Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Romans Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Romans 6:9 say about Christ's relationship with death?
options: Death hath no more dominion over him.
He has no relationship with death.
questions.correctAnswer: Death hath no more dominion over him.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:9 states that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him, indicating His victory over death.

questions.question: What does Romans 6:11 promise will happen if someone reckons themselves dead to sin?
options: They will be alive unto God through Jesus Christ.
questions.correctAnswer: They will be alive unto God through Jesus Christ.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:11 instructs to reckon yourselves dead unto sin, promising that doing so leads to being alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

questions.question: What should we not let reign in our mortal body according to Romans 6:12?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:12 admonishes not to let sin reign in your mortal body, emphasizing the need for self-control against sinful desires.

questions.question: What does Romans 6:13 say we should yield our members as?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:13 encourages yielding your members as instruments of righteousness unto God, promoting a life aligned with God's will.

questions.question: According to Romans 6:14, what shall not have dominion over you?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:14 declares that sin shall not have dominion over you because you are not under the law, but under grace, highlighting the transformative power of grace.

questions.question: What is Paul's response in Romans 6:15 regarding sinning because we are under grace?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:15 states 'God forbid' in response to the idea of sinning because of grace, emphasizing the serious nature of sin even under grace.

questions.question: What does Romans 6:16 teach about yielding ourselves?
options: We become servants to whom we obey.
It doesn't matter who we obey.
questions.correctAnswer: We become servants to whom we obey.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:16 explains that yielding ourselves as servants to obey means we become servants to whatever we obey, whether it leads to sin or righteousness.

questions.question: What does Romans 6:3 say about baptism into Jesus Christ?
options: It means being baptized into his death.
questions.correctAnswer: It means being baptized into his death.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:3 clarifies that being baptized into Jesus Christ signifies being baptized into his death, symbolizing identification with His sacrifice.

questions.question: According to Romans 6:6, what happens to our old man?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:6 states that our old man is crucified with Him, indicating the destruction of the body of sin and the end of serving sin.

questions.question: What assurance does Romans 6:8 give about being dead with Christ?
options: We shall also live with Him.
questions.correctAnswer: We shall also live with Him.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:8 assures that if we are dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with Him, pointing to the hope of eternal life.

questions.question: What does Romans 6:4 state about walking in newness of life?
options: It follows being buried with Him by baptism into death.
It is only for the righteous.
questions.correctAnswer: It follows being buried with Him by baptism into death.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:4 establishes that walking in newness of life is a result of being buried with Christ, highlighting the transformative power of baptism.

questions.question: Those who have been planted together in the likeness of His death will also be in the likeness of what, according to Romans 6:5?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:5 states that if we have been planted together in the likeness of His death, we shall be also in the likeness of His resurrection, indicating a shared experience in Christ.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 6:1 asks if we should continue in sin so that grace may abound.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:1 asks the rhetorical question about continuing in sin for grace to abound, setting up the discussion on sin and grace.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 6:7 states that he that is dead is still bound by sin.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:7 clarifies that he that is dead is freed from sin, indicating liberation from the bondage of sin through death.

questions.question: True or False: According to Romans 6:10, Christ lives unto God.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:10 states that Christ liveth, he liveth unto God, affirming His eternal life and purpose in relation to God, which makes the statement true.

hard.title: Romans Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Romans Chapter 6.

questions.question: What were the Romans before they obeyed from the heart?
questions.explanation: They were servants of sin, as stated in Romans 6:17.

questions.question: What have the Romans become after being made free from sin?
questions.explanation: They became servants to God after being made free from sin, as stated in Romans 6:22.

questions.question: What is the end of things that the Romans are now ashamed of?
questions.explanation: The end of those things is death, as stated in Romans 6:21.

questions.question: What fruit do the Romans have now that they are made free from sin?
questions.explanation: They have their fruit unto holiness, as stated in Romans 6:22.

questions.question: What does Romans 6:23 say the wages of sin is?
questions.explanation: The wages of sin is death, as stated in Romans 6:23.

questions.question: What is the gift of God according to Romans 6:23?
questions.explanation: The gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ, as stated in Romans 6:23.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'doulos' in Romans 6:18 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Doulos' means servant, which is used in the context of Romans 6:18 to describe the believers' relationship to righteousness.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Romans 6:17 with the phrase 'obeyed from the heart'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'obeyed from the heart' is a metaphor for genuine commitment and transformation.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects with the theme of being made free from sin?
questions.explanation: John 8:36 states, 'If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed,' connecting with the theme of freedom from sin.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of the wages of sin being death?
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:8 discusses the second death and contrasts it with eternal life, which is relevant to the wages of sin being death.

questions.question: What comes before Romans 6:17?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:16 comes immediately before Romans 6:17, discussing the concept of servanthood and obedience.

questions.question: What does Romans 6:6 imply about the old man?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:6 states that our old man is crucified with him, indicating a complete break from the old self.

questions.question: What does Romans 6:14 state about sin's dominion over believers?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:14 clearly states that sin shall not have dominion over believers since they are under grace.

questions.question: True or False: Believers are encouraged to continue in sin so that grace may abound.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:2 states, 'God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?'

questions.question: True or False: The end of those things whereof the Romans are now ashamed is life.
questions.explanation: Romans 6:21 states that the end of those things is death, not life.

theological.title: Romans Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Romans Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 6:2 teach about the believer's relationship to sin?
options: Believers are dead to sin and must no longer live in it
Believers are justified but still slaves to sin
Believers may continue sinning because grace covers all
Believers should ignore sin since it cannot affect them
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are dead to sin and must no longer live in it
questions.explanation: Romans 6:2 states, "How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?" indicating the believer's death to sin and the necessity to no longer live in it.

questions.question: What doctrine about baptism and union with Christ is taught in Romans 6:3?
options: Baptism symbolizes a believer's union with Christ's death
Baptism is a ritual cleansing without spiritual significance
Baptism guarantees automatic salvation regardless of faith
Baptism is primarily a public declaration without inward change
questions.correctAnswer: Baptism symbolizes a believer's union with Christ's death
questions.explanation: Romans 6:3 says, "Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?" teaching baptism as a symbol of union with Christ's death.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the believer's 'old man' is taught in Romans 6:6?
options: The old man is crucified with Christ so the body of sin is destroyed
The old man remains active and must be tolerated
The old man is inferior but still retains power over the believer
The old man is only symbolically crucified without real effect
questions.correctAnswer: The old man is crucified with Christ so the body of sin is destroyed
questions.explanation: Romans 6:6 teaches that "our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed," indicating a definitive break from sin's dominion.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 6:9 specifically demonstrate in regard to Christ's resurrection?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:9 states that "Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him," demonstrating God's immutability in that Christ's victory over death is permanent.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Romans 6:14 regarding believers' freedom from sin's dominion?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:14 states, "For ye are not under the law, but under grace," emphasizing God's grace as the basis for freedom from sin's dominion.

questions.question: How does Romans 6:4 prepare for the New Testament theme of sanctification?
options: By teaching believers to walk in newness of life after being raised with Christ
By emphasizing legalistic adherence to the Mosaic Law
By denying the necessity of moral transformation
By focusing solely on justification without sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: By teaching believers to walk in newness of life after being raised with Christ
questions.explanation: Romans 6:4 says believers are "buried with him... that even so we also should walk in newness of life," linking union with Christ’s resurrection to sanctification.

questions.question: How does Romans 6:23 connect to the broader biblical narrative of salvation?
options: It contrasts the wages of sin (death) with God's gift of eternal life through Christ
It teaches that eternal life is earned by works
It suggests sin has no real consequences
It teaches universal salvation regardless of faith
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts the wages of sin (death) with God's gift of eternal life through Christ
questions.explanation: Romans 6:23 contrasts "the wages of sin is death" with "the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ," aligning with the gospel message of salvation by grace.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 6:11 and Romans 6:13 teach about sanctification?
options: Believers are to reckon themselves dead to sin but alive to God, and yield their members as instruments of righteousness
Believers should ignore sin because it has no power
Believers are only partially sanctified and must rely on the law
Believers must earn righteousness through works apart from Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are to reckon themselves dead to sin but alive to God, and yield their members as instruments of righteousness
questions.explanation: Romans 6:11 instructs to "reckon yourselves dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God," and 6:13 commands to "yield yourselves unto God... as instruments of righteousness," teaching active sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 6:16 and Romans 6:18 teach about servitude and righteousness?
options: Believers who yield to righteousness become servants of God, contrasting former servitude to sin
Believers remain slaves to sin even after conversion
Servitude to God is optional for believers
Obedience to righteousness is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Believers who yield to righteousness become servants of God, contrasting former servitude to sin
questions.explanation: Romans 6:16 explains that to whom one yields as a servant, one obeys, and 6:18 states believers "became the servants of righteousness," highlighting sanctified servitude.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 6:20 and Romans 6:21 teach about the consequences of previous sin?
options: Being servants of sin meant being free from righteousness and leading to death
Servitude to sin had no real effect on spiritual condition
Sinful actions resulted in immediate forgiveness without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Being servants of sin meant being free from righteousness and leading to death
questions.explanation: Romans 6:20 states, "when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness," and 6:21 notes the fruit of that servitude was death, emphasizing sin’s deadly consequence.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Romans 6:1-2 teaches that grace encourages sinning. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Grace does not encourage sin; believers are dead to sin and must not continue in it
Grace gives believers a license to sin without consequence
Sin is irrelevant because grace covers all actions automatically
Believers can sin freely because the law no longer applies
questions.correctAnswer: Grace does not encourage sin; believers are dead to sin and must not continue in it
questions.explanation: Romans 6:1-2 asks if we should continue in sin that grace may abound and answers "God forbid" because believers are dead to sin and must not live in it, opposing the claim that grace encourages sin.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 6:17 teach about spiritual transformation?
options: Believers obey the form of doctrine from the heart, indicating genuine inward change
Obedience is merely external and superficial
Transformation is unnecessary since believers remain servants of sin
Doctrine is irrelevant to spiritual life
questions.correctAnswer: Believers obey the form of doctrine from the heart, indicating genuine inward change
questions.explanation: Romans 6:17 says believers "have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you," teaching heartfelt obedience and transformation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Romans 6:10 in relation to Christ's life and death?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:10 states that Christ "died unto sin once" and "liveth unto God," emphasizing His holiness in being set apart from sin and living unto God.

questions.question: How does Romans 6:12 illustrate the practical outworking of sanctification?
options: Believers must not let sin reign in their mortal bodies or obey its lusts
Believers should accept sin as unavoidable
Sin is only a theoretical problem, not practical
Obedience to sin is part of Christian freedom
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must not let sin reign in their mortal bodies or obey its lusts
questions.explanation: Romans 6:12 commands, "Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof," showing sanctification's practical call to resist sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 6:5 and Romans 6:8 teach about resurrection life in Christ?
options: Believers are united with Christ in both death and resurrection, promising life with Him
Believers only experience Christ's death but not resurrection
Resurrection life is metaphorical and not actual
Believers remain spiritually dead despite union with Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are united with Christ in both death and resurrection, promising life with Him
questions.explanation: Romans 6:5 speaks of being planted in the likeness of Christ's death and resurrection, and 6:8 affirms belief that if we are dead with Christ, we shall also live with Him, teaching union with Christ's resurrection life.
